testing_centers.notes: ACP (Creative Cloud) exams delivered via Certiport at authorized test centers.
Adobe Experience Cloud professional/expert exams (AD0-E series) delivered via Pearson VUE. Online proctoring available.

id_requirements: One government-issued photo ID with full name. Name must match registration exactly.
exam_rules: Closed-book. No notes or reference materials. ACP exams include both multiple-choice questions and performance-based tasks in a simulated application environment. AD0-E series exams are multiple-choice only.
renewal_options: ACP (Creative Cloud) certifications are version-specific and do not expire but may become outdated with new software versions. Adobe Experience Cloud certifications (AD0-E series) are valid for 2 years; renewal by passing a current renewal exam at no charge.

prerequisites.description: Minimum 2 years experience with Adobe Analytics; familiarity with digital analytics and reporting

retake_policy.notes: 30-day waiting period between attempts. Full exam fee required for retake. Third and subsequent attempts require 14-day waiting period.

editorial.meta_description: AD0-E212 Adobe Analytics Business Practitioner exam tests segmentation, reporting, variables, implementation and integrations. $225, 50 questions, 120‑minute.
editorial.overview: Adobe’s AD0-E212 Business Practitioner certification confirms you can work with Adobe Analytics to create segments, generate reports, configure variables, manage implementations, handle admin tasks, and integrate with other Adobe solutions. The exam is administered by Adobe, delivered as a linear computer‑based test, and remains current. It consists of 50 questions to be answered in 120 minutes, and a passing score of 72 percent is required.
editorial.who_should_take: Analytics managers, report developers, digital marketers, and implementation specialists who have hands‑on experience building segments, configuring reports, and managing Adobe Analytics environments should pursue this credential. The exam validates their ability to apply best practices across six core domains of Adobe Analytics.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review Adobe’s official exam guide and study the segmentation, reporting, variable, implementation, admin and integration sections on Experience League. Practice building segments in the Segment builder, creating reports in Analysis Workspace, and configuring variables via the Admin Console. Take sample performance‑based tasks, time yourself for 120 minutes, and aim for at least 72 % correct.

domain_guidance.summary: Focuses on building and managing audience segments using the Segment builder, nested containers, and sequential logic. Understand visitor, visit and hit level hierarchies, AND/OR operators, tagging, sharing, and how segments apply across reports and Analysis Workspace.

Covers creation and interpretation of reports, dashboards and visualizations in Analysis Workspace. Includes selecting metrics, dimensions, applying segments, using freeform tables, and exporting insights as PDFs or CSVs for stakeholder communication.

Focuses on eVars, props, events and config variables, their syntax, scope and mapping to data layers. Explains the order of operations, tracking functions like t() and clearVars(), and best practices for accurate data collection.

Addresses overall implementation strategies, including tag deployment, data layer design, and integration with Adobe Experience Platform. Emphasizes testing, validation and troubleshooting to ensure data integrity across web and mobile properties.

Focuses on user and permission management in the Adobe Admin Console and Analytics Admin Tools. Includes report suite configuration, variable and classification settings, and governance processes for segment sharing and approval.

Explores how Adobe Analytics connects with other Adobe Experience Cloud products, data warehouses and third‑party tools. Covers data export, API usage and best practices for maintaining consistent metrics across integrated solutions.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive early, ensure a stable internet connection, and have your Adobe ID ready. Allocate the full 120 minutes, read each question carefully, and flag items to review. Keep track of the 72 % passing threshold as you progress.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The AD0‑E212 exam contains 50 multiple‑choice and performance‑based questions. You will encounter a mix of standard items and tasks that simulate real‑world Adobe Analytics scenarios, all delivered in a linear computer‑based format.

The required passing score is 72 percent. You must answer enough questions correctly to achieve this threshold out of the 50 total items. Scores are calculated automatically at the end of the 120‑minute session.
The exam duration is 120 minutes. It is a timed, linear test administered via Pearson VUE. Manage your time wisely to answer all 50 questions within the allotted period.

faq.question_title: What topics are covered in AD0‑E212?
faq.answer_text: The exam covers six domains: Segmentation, Reporting, Variables & Implementation, Implementation Knowledge, Admin Concepts, and Analytics Integrations. Each domain contributes a specific weight to the overall score, reflecting its importance in Adobe Analytics practice.

methodology.summary: Content was assembled by extracting domain weights, exam logistics and study topics from Adobe’s official exam guide, certification page and Experience League documentation, then organized into concise editorial sections.
